s01.t02: Smartlead is the sending tool in our cold email stack. This guide covers what happens after your domains and inboxes exist: connecting them, warming them up, setting limits, and launching the first sequence without burning a domain.
s01.t04: Warm-up emails a day at the start
s01.t05: Live emails per inbox per day
s01.t08: Add each inbox in Smartlead's email accounts section using Google sign-in. If your Workspace admin restricts third-party apps, allow Smartlead as a trusted app in the Admin console's API controls first, or the connection will fail.
s01.t09: Connect every inbox you set up, not just one per domain. Each inbox gets its own warm-up and sending limit, which is how volume spreads safely.
s01.t10: Haven't set up domains and inboxes yet? Start with our cold email infrastructure guide, then come back here.
s01.t11: Turn on warm-up for every inbox
s01.t12: Warm-up sends and replies to a small number of emails between real inboxes, so mailbox providers learn to trust a new address. Start at 3 to 5 warm-up emails per inbox per day and ramp up by 2 to 3 a day until you reach a steady 20 to 30.
s01.t13: Give every new inbox 14 to 21 days of warm-up before its first live email, and leave warm-up running after the campaign starts.
s01.t15: Cap live sending at about 30 emails per inbox per day, and stay under 40. Volume comes from more inboxes, not more email per inbox: our standard 40 inboxes send up to about 1,200 emails a day at that rate.
s01.t16: In the first week of live sending, start lower and raise the limit as replies come in and bounces stay low.
s01.t18: Verify every address before it goes into Smartlead; we use BounceBan. Bounces are one of the fastest ways to damage a new domain, and a list that looks clean in a spreadsheet often isn't.
s01.t19: Upload the list as a CSV with first name, company and any personalisation fields your copy uses, and map each column to a Smartlead variable so placeholders like {{first_name}} fill in correctly.
s01.t21: Write in plain text and keep links to a minimum. Space the emails out: a workable cadence is day 1, day 3, day 7, day 12 and day 18. Write two variants of the first email to test against each other.
s01.t23:
Email 1: day 1  - the observation, one question, no calendar link
Email 2: day 3  - the cost of the problem
Email 3: day 7  - one short, real proof point
Email 4: day 12 - something useful, no ask
Email 5: day 18 - a polite close-the-loop
s01.t24: Schedule sends in the prospect's time zone
s01.t25: Set the sending window to the prospect's working hours on weekdays, not yours. For an India-based team selling to the US, that means sending while you sleep. Smartlead spreads emails across the window with a gap between each send, so they don't go out in one burst.
s01.t27: Stop the sequence for a lead as soon as they reply. Include a simple way to opt out, honour every request within 2 days and never re-add a suppressed contact.
s01.t28: If you track opens, set up a custom tracking domain, since shared tracking links can hurt deliverability. Many teams turn open tracking off and judge campaigns on replies and meetings instead.
s01.t29: Launch small and watch the numbers
s01.t30: Launch to a small part of the list first. Keep the spam complaint rate below 0.3%, which is the limit Gmail and Yahoo set; Google recommends staying below 0.1%. If bounces or complaints rise on an inbox, pause it and fix the list or copy before sending more.
s01.t31: Judge the campaign on positive replies and meetings booked. Across our campaigns, 1% to 3% of prospects reply, and at least 20% of those replies are positive.
s01.t32: Every inbox is connected and has warmed up for 14 to 21 days, with warm-up still on.
s01.t33: Live sending is capped at about 30 emails per inbox per day.
s01.t34: The list is verified, and every placeholder in the copy maps to a filled column.
s01.t35: The sequence is plain text, spaced over 18 days, with two first-email variants.
s01.t36: Sends are scheduled for the prospect's weekday working hours.
s01.t37: Replies stop the sequence, and opt-outs are honoured within 2 days.
